items.headline: Killers guitarist Dave Keuning says a major stroke nearly killed him
items.summary: he wrote on Thanksgiving that a blood clot cut off blood flow to the right side of his brain about two weeks earlier, that doctors gave him a 40% chance of survival, and that he went straight into surgery.
items.matters: he says he can play guitar as well as before and has full use of his hands, feet and speech, and the band now has a guitarist back after a close call; he and his wife had a baby daughter, Odette, about three months ago.
items.body:
Killers guitarist Dave Keuning shared both beautiful and terrifying news yesterday. In an Instagram post, Keuning revealed that, three months ago, he and his wife had a baby girl, Odette. Then, a couple of weeks ago, Keuning survived a major stroke. Thankfully, he and his wife were able to rush to the hospital, and he was immediately taken into surgery. He shared that the doctors said he had "a 40% chance of survival and I would have disabilities after, but by some miracle I am fine."

He added: "I feel extremely fortunate that I am alive and well, and that I can use my hands and feet and talk just like before. I am thankful for my wife, my son, my daughter, and all of my bandmates, who I feel closer to than ever."

Two weeks ago, I had a major stroke, and thanks to my wife acting fast, I went straight to the hospital and into surgery. The first hour after a stroke is critical when it comes to getting to the hospital. I had a blood clot in my brain that cut off the blood supply to the entire right side of my brain. By the time I arrived at the hospital, I was blind in one eye and had lost function on my left side, but I still wasn’t able to realize I was having a stroke. The doctors said I had a 40% chance or survival and I would have disabilities after, but by some miracle I am fine.

And yes I can play guitar just as good as before. It was the first thing I checked when I woke up from surgery.

I feel extremely fortunate that I am alive and well, and that I can use my hands and feet and talk just like before. I am thankful for my wife, my son, my daughter, and all of my bandmates, who I feel closer to than ever.

Think of it as a series of bite-sized soap opera episodes built for the scrolling culture of social media. Both the album and the series will reportedly share the same title: The Trouble With The Truth.

The scripted microdrama, which will star Gray, is currently casting. The plan is to release both the album and series in Q1, with production scheduled to begin in January 2027.

I'd just like to share a few titles: My Ex Called Me Fat, The Vampire Lord Called Me His, My Billionaire Divorce Squad, Bully Me? I Run The Mob, and Crypto Jackpot After Life Failure.

Microdramas first began gaining traction in China during the 2010s, and the business has continued to expand. Deloitte projects that in-app microdrama revenue will reach approximately $7.8 billion in 2026.

items.headline: Westminster council approves the Beatles attraction at 3 Savile Row
items.summary: the planning committee cleared "The Beatles at 3 Savile Row" on 24 November, with archive exhibitions, a recreated basement studio and rooftop access, at the former Apple Corps HQ where the band played its last public show in January 1969.
items.matters: it is expected to open in 2027 and could host up to 1,140 visitors a day at weekends, though draft conditions banned live music on the rooftop terrace.
items.body:
Westminster City Council has approved plans for a Beatles visitor attraction at 3 Savile Row, the former London headquarters of Apple Corps.

Apple Corps, which manages The Beatles ‘ creative and business interests, first unveiled the project in May under the name The Beatles at 3 Savile Row.

According to the council, the plans cover exhibitions drawn from the Apple Corps archives, a recreated version of the basement recording studio, and access to the rooftop.

On January 30 that year, John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr, joined by Billy Preston, played on the building’s roof.

The concert was later featured in Peter Jackson ‘s 2021 documentary Get Back, which won five Emmy Awards.

“This is Fab news for fans of the Fab-Four, and for Westminster,” said Tim Barnes, Deputy Leader of Westminster City Council and its Cabinet Member for Growth and Planning.

“ 3 Savile Row has an extraordinary place in British music history. This is where the Beatles worked, recorded, and ultimately played their final public performance on a rooftop above the streets of Mayfair.

“We’re incredibly proud of Westminster ‘s cultural heritage and we want to see historic places like this continue to play a part in the life of our city. These plans will give fans from around the world the opportunity to get back to where a remarkable piece of music history actually happened.

“Huge work has taken place to develop the plans for a Beatles Experience at 3 Savile Row and we’re delighted to keep moving forward after [Tuesday’s] hearing,” said Tom Greene, CEO of Apple Corps.

“We’re especially excited to show fans what we have in store for the world-renowned rooftop, where visitors will feel that they are sitting behind The Beatles as they played their fabled final show, before stepping outside onto probably the most famous terrace in the world.

Greene also addressed the committee in a speech, a copy of which has been seen by MBW.

He also pointed to a letter Paul McCartney sent to the committee about how much the building means to him personally.

“We would like to return the front part of the building where the heritage remains intact to how it would have looked and felt in 1969 right down to the Apple green carpet – and supplement this with the latest AV technologies to deliver a truly immersive experience for fans of The Beatles,” Greene told the committee.

The company will run a cafe and bar in the basement in the evenings, open to ticket holders only and built around a recreation of the recording studio, Greene said.

items.headline: Mary Bono asks the Ninth Circuit to overturn Cher's win in the Sonny Bono royalties fight
items.summary: her opening brief, filed 24 November, argues all reclaimed US rights belong to the heirs, after a judge awarded Cher over $187,000 in withheld royalties plus interest.
items.matters: the case tests whether copyright terminations can wipe out a divorce-settlement royalty share, and Cher has appealed the denial of her legal fees, so both appeals are now consolidated.
items.body:
Mary Bono, the widow of Sonny Bono, has asked a federal appeals court to overturn Cher’s win in their fight over royalties from Sonny’s songs.

A federal judge ruled in November 2025 that Cher remains entitled to half of Sonny’s income from songs he wrote before February 1, 1974, including I Got You Babe.

Mary Bono’s lawyers at Donahue Fitzgerald filed her opening brief with the US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit on Tuesday (November 24).

The brief asks the court to rule that the US rights and royalties in those songs now belong to Sonny’s widow and four children “free and clear” of the rights granted to Cher under the pair’s 1978 divorce settlement.

His heirs are Mary Bono and his four children, Christine, Chaz (Sonny and Cher’s son), Chesare, and Chianna.

US copyright law lets songwriters, or their surviving spouses and children, reclaim rights the songwriters signed away decades earlier through a process known as termination.

In 2016, Mary Bono, Chesare, and Chianna served notice reclaiming, on behalf of all five heirs, the rights Sonny had granted to his music publishers in 1966.

The heirs then stopped paying Cher her 50% share of the heirs’ US royalty income from the songs, arguing that the reclaimed rights belonged entirely to them.

Cher sued Mary Bono in October 2021, claiming a continued right to 50% of all of the heirs’ income from the songs.

In a final judgment on November 26, 2025, US District Judge John A. Kronstadt of the Central District of California ruled largely in Cher’s favor, as MBW reported at the time.

In July 2026, he denied Cher’s request for attorneys’ fees. Cher has appealed that decision, and the Ninth Circuit has consolidated her appeal with Mary Bono’s.

The brief sets out how every $1 of income from most of the songs was divided while Sonny was alive and acting as his own royalty administrator.

Sonny received 38.5 cents: a 7-cent administration fee, plus half of the remaining 63 cents.

Judge Kronstadt’s ruling leaves Cher with half of all of the heirs’ income from the songs, including the reclaimed publishers’ share, after the administration fee and certain costs.

By MBW ‘s calculation, that would give her around 45 cents of each dollar before those costs, up from 31.5 cents.

Mary Bono’s brief does not put a total dollar figure on the royalties in dispute.

Her main argument is that all of the reclaimed rights, including future royalties, belong to Sonny’s heirs alone.

If the appeals court agrees, Cher would lose her share of the US royalties from the songs.

items.headline: Baltimore sues Vivid Seats over drip pricing
items.summary: the city's 23 November suit alleges misleading search ads, prices that rose across checkout screens, bundled per-ticket prices and fees shown late, and cites a J. Cole ticket advertised at $156 that cost $238.
items.matters: Vivid Seats denies the claims and says it has shown all-in pricing since May 2025, and the case adds to pressure on resale platforms, including a Washington D.C. 10% resale price cap due on 1 January 2027 that Vivid Seats and others are suing to block.
items.body:
The lawsuit, brought under the City ‘s Consumer Protection Ordinance, was filed in the Circuit Court for Baltimore City on Monday (November 23).

It is also seeking civil penalties for each violation, plus attorneys’ fees and costs, though the City ‘s announcement does not put a figure on the penalties.

According to the City, a pre-suit investigation into Baltimore events listed on the platform identified four practices.

The second is drip pricing. The price on Vivid Seats ‘ own pages allegedly climbs screen by screen as a buyer works through checkout.

The third involves bundling: the City claims some per-ticket prices on Vivid Seats applied only to customers buying at least two tickets.

Buyers only learned of that minimum near the end of the purchase, the City alleges.

The fourth concerns mandatory service and delivery fees, which the City alleges were, until at least April 2026, shown only after a buyer moved past the first page.

Those fees were not broken down line by line until the final checkout screen, according to the City.

The complaint cites examples from four shows in Baltimore, featuring J. Cole, BTS, Megan Moroney, and Trevor Noah, according to the Baltimore Sun, which reviewed the filing.

It argues that buyers who have already sunk time into choosing seats tend to stick with a purchase even as the total goes up, and that Vivid Seats designs its checkout around that habit.

“ Vivid Seats knowingly deceives buyers by exploiting these cognitive biases, drawing on years of transactional and engagement data,” the complaint alleges, according to the Sun.

“ Vivid Seats effectuates this deception through a combination of what the Federal Trade Commission (‘FTC’) calls ‘digital dark patterns,’ all of which are intended to manipulate consumers into spending more money than they otherwise would on tickets,” the complaint adds.

The term refers to website and app designs that steer users toward choices they might not otherwise make. The FTC examined such designs in a 2022 report, Bringing Dark Patterns to Light.

“ Vivid Seats has profited from these unfair and deceptive trade practices,” the complaint also claims, per the Sun.

The company charges sellers a 10% commission on every resale and also takes fees from buyers, according to the City ‘s announcement.

items.headline: Worth watching this week: Disney's "Hexed", in cinemas since 25 November
items.summary: Walt Disney Animation's witch adventure holds 68% from critics and 87% from audiences on Rotten Tomatoes, with an A- CinemaScore.
items.matters: it is heading for roughly a $34m five-day holiday weekend against a $200m budget before marketing, so the reception is stronger than the takings so far.
items.body:
Among the new releases, “Focker-in-Law” is in the No. 2 spot with $7.7 million grossed on Thursday, bringing its running Thanksgiving opening weekend total to $13 million as it is estimated to open to a $40 million 5-day opening, matching pre-release projections.

Starring Ben Stiller, Robert De Niro and series newcomer Ariana Grande, the fourth installment of the “Meet the Parents” comedy series has a $90 million budget co-financed by Universal and Paramount and is projected to make around $30 million overseas this weekend. Critics weren’t impressed with a 31% Rotten Tomatoes score, but fans of the series and Grande are more positive with an 86% RT audience score and a B+ on CinemaScore.

While Disney has made more attempts to break general and family audience reluctance towards original theatrical animation than other studios like Illumination and DreamWorks, its larger budgets have made the misfires like “Wish” and “Strange World” more costly.

The good news is that reception for “Hexed” has been somewhat more positive than “Wish” with RT scores of 68% critics and 87% audience to go with an A- on CinemaScore and 62% “definite recommend” score on PostTrak. But if “Hexed” can’t draw better holdover interest off that word-of-mouth than “Wish,” it will mean that Disney will have to turn to “Avengers: Doomsday” and its anticipated historic box office haul to recoup any losses.

items.headline: Villeneuve is "deeply disappointed" that "Dune: Part Three" opens on 18 December, the same day as "Avengers: Doomsday"
items.summary: he told Time the studio was committed to the date with IMAX and could not move it.
items.matters: fans are calling the day "Dunesday", and he says it could be one of the biggest box-office weekends of all time.
items.body:
Hollywood may have another “Barbenheimer” phenomenon on its hands this December, but “Dune: Part Three” director Denis Villeneuve is not celebrating it.

The filmmaker’s third and final installment in his massive “Dune” sci-fi trilogy is set to hit theaters on Dec. 18, the same day Marvel and Disney are slated to release “Avengers: Doomsday.” The two films’ shared release date has led many on the internet to coin Dec. 18 this year as “Dunesday” in an attempt to encourage moviegoers to go see both “Dune: Part Three” and “Avengers: Doomsday” in theaters the same weekend.

An adaptation of author Frank Herbert’s second “Dune” novel, “Dune Messiah,” Villeneuve’s new film is being positioned as the massive, climactic final chapter in his sci-fi trilogy. As such, many of the franchise’s core stars are back for “Part Three,” including Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Jason Momoa, Florence Pugh and (in a much more expanded role) Anya Taylor-Joy.

Robert Pattinson, who was chosen by Villeneuve this month to play James Bond in his forthcoming 007 reboot, also has a key role in “Dune: Part Three” as a shape-shifter plotting an assassination attempt on Chalamet’s Paul Atreides.

Speaking further with Time, Villeneuve expressed hope that “Dune: Part Three” may not be overwhelmed by the enormous popularity of its Marvel competitor.

items.headline: "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" is No. 1 on Netflix in 37 of 38 countries, with no US date
items.summary: it began streaming internationally on 26 November, 118 days after its theatrical debut, and has grossed over $2.5bn worldwide.
items.matters: the UK, Canada and Australia are held back by existing deals, Netflix and Sony have not confirmed a US date, and Sony's extended-cut theatrical re-release on 4 December makes an early US streaming date less likely.
items.body:
The biggest movie of 2026 has quietly swung onto Netflix in nearly 40 countries this week, and it has gone straight to number one almost everywhere. If you’re in the United States, though, you’re still waiting, and Netflix has yet to confirm when Spider-Man: Brand New Day will arrive.

Back in July, we predicted that Tom Holland’s fourth solo outing would hit Netflix US around November 28th, 2026, based on the usual 120-day gap between a Sony movie’s theatrical debut and its Netflix arrival. We also warned that date could slip. With November 28th now upon us and no sign of the movie on Netflix US, it looks like the later scenario is the one playing out.

The international rollout, on the other hand, has turned out far bigger than we expected.

Brand New Day began arriving on Netflix on November 26th, just 118 days after it hit theaters, with a few more regions (including Malaysia, Thailand, and Ukraine, per uNoGS) following on November 27th.

According to FlixPatrol’s daily top 10 data, the movie is now charting in 38 countries. Here’s where it’s featured so far:

Unsurprisingly, it’s been an instant hit. The movie debuted at number one on day one in Hong Kong, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, and Taiwan. By day two, it had climbed to the top spot in 37 of the 38 countries, with Indonesia (where it sits at number two) the lone holdout.

Some of those jumps were dramatic. In Cyprus, Switzerland, and Ukraine, it leapt from tenth to first overnight, while Belgium, Finland, Iceland, Malta, the Netherlands, and Norway saw it enter the charts directly at number one.

That’s hardly a shock for a movie that grossed over $2.5 billion at the global box office, making it the highest-grossing movie ever in the US and the third biggest of all time worldwide, per Deadline.

Here’s the part that caught us off guard. In our original prediction, we only expected a handful of Asian markets with existing first-window arrangements (India, Singapore, Malaysia, and the Philippines) to get Brand New Day on a similar timeline to the US. Those all came good.

What we didn’t expect was the movie turning up across much of Europe. We’d pegged most European regions for a wait of 18 to 24 months, given Sony’s patchwork of local first-window deals.

Our understanding was that Netflix’s new global Pay-1 deal with Sony Pictures only applied to theatrical releases from 2027 onwards, which would’ve made Brand New Day the last Spider-Man movie stuck on the old fragmented schedule. items.headline: All four seasons of "Eastbound & Down" arrive on Netflix in the US on 12 December
items.summary: the 29 episodes of Danny McBride's HBO comedy (2009–2013) hold a 91% average on Rotten Tomatoes.
items.matters: it is a US-only licence that will probably stay on HBO Max too, and recent HBO deals on Netflix have usually run 12 to 18 months or less.
items.body:
HBO’s back catalog continues to trickle onto Netflix, and the next pickup is one of the network’s best-loved comedies. All four seasons of Eastbound & Down will begin streaming on Netflix in the United States on December 12th, 2026, although, as always, it’ll only be sticking around for a limited time.

First listed in our December 2026 preview, the pickup covers the show’s entire run, which aired on HBO between February 2009 and November 2013. As it stands, this is a US-only addition, and we’d expect the series to remain on HBO Max throughout its Netflix stint, as has been the case with every HBO pickup so far.

For the uninitiated, Eastbound & Down stars Danny McBride as Kenny Powers, a loud, crude and endlessly self-regarding former Major League pitcher whose career has gone up in smoke. With nowhere else to go, he heads home to North Carolina and takes a job as a substitute PE teacher at his old middle school, all while convinced the big leagues will come calling again. Later seasons take Kenny to Mexico and Myrtle Beach.

The series was created by McBride, Jody Hill and the late Ben Best, with Will Ferrell and Adam McKay among the executive producers. Ferrell also pops up on screen as car dealer Ashley Schaeffer. Steve Little, Katy Mixon, John Hawkes and Jennifer Irwin lead the supporting cast, and the guest list across the four seasons includes Michael Peña, Jason Sudeikis, Ken Marino, Tim Heidecker, Jillian Bell and Matthew McConaughey.

It was never a ratings monster for HBO (the final season averaged around 780,000 viewers, per TV Series Finale), but its reputation has only grown since. It holds a 91% average on Rotten Tomatoes, which also placed it on its list of the 200 best comedy series of all time. More importantly, it kicked off McBride’s long partnership with HBO, which went on to produce Vice Principals and The Righteous Gemstones.

Fun fact: the show was supposed to end after season 3, only for McBride and Hill to return for one more round. HBO was less keen on going further, with McBride later revealing the network passed on two spin-offs, including one built around Ferrell’s Ashley Schaeffer.

If you’d told us before 2023 that HBO Originals would be streaming on Netflix, we wouldn’t have believed you. That changed in the summer of 2023 when Insecure arrived, swiftly followed by Ballers, Band of Brothers and The Pacific and Six Feet Under.

items.headline: Joel Coen's "Jack of Spades" will get a theatrical run in autumn 2027 before Netflix
items.summary: the Scottish Highlands gothic mystery stars Josh O'Connor, Patsy Ferran, Damian Lewis, Lesley Manville and Frances McDormand.
items.matters: the release is timed ahead of awards season and is Coen's first Netflix film since "The Ballad of Buster Scruggs" (2018), made with his brother; no streaming date has been announced.
items.body:
Netflix has secured the rights to 'Jack of Spades', a sinister new Coen brothers project eyeing an awards season theatrical run before hitting the streamer in late 2027.

Joel Coen’s gothic drama film Jack of Spades was picked up by Netflix earlier this month and is set for a theatrical release in Autumn 2027, ahead of the award season and its streaming debut. Starring in Jack of Spades are Patsy Ferran, Josh O’Connor, Damian Lewis, Lesley Manville, and Frances McDormand. Here’s everything we know so far about Jack of Spades on Netflix.

Jack of Spades is an upcoming Netflix Original period gothic-drama film directed by Joel Coen, who wrote it alongside his longtime collaborator and brother, Ethan Coen, as well as Eleanor Catton and Connor McPherson. While both brothers have directed solo projects in recent years, the film marks a rare dynamic where Joel takes sole directing duties while Ethan remains on board as a co-writer.

Joel is also a producer on the film, alongside Robert Graf and Frances McDormand, and Steven Rales for Indian Paintbrush. Graham Broadbent and Pete Czernin are producers through Blueprint Pictures. Donald MacKinnon is the executive producer.

On November 2, 2026, it was confirmed that Netflix had acquired the rights to Jack of Spades. This is the second time Netflix has worked with Joel Coen, who previously wrote, directed, and produced the 2018 comedy The Ballad of Buster Scruggs alongside his brother.

A sinister gothic mystery filled with intrigue and betrayal set in the atmospheric Scottish Highlands.

Josh O’Connor (Wake Up Dead Man), Patsy Ferran (Living), Frances McDormand (Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri), Lesley Manville (Phantom Thread), and Damian Lewis (Band of Brothers) are the film’s leads.

Other cast members listed so far are: Ian Barritt (Life of Mars), Kris Hitchen (Sorry We Missed You), Finbar Lynch (Child 44), Aaron MacGregor (Kensuke’s Kingdom), and John McManus (Miss Saigon).

Filming for Jack of Spades reportedly took place between June 2025 and November 2025, in various locations across Scotland, including Paisley, Edinburgh, Culross, and Glasgow.

Netflix has yet to confirm an official release date or window for the film. However, it has confirmed that Jack of Spades will receive a theatrical release in Autumn 2027.

This likely means we’ll see Jack of Spades on Netflix sometime after, so expect a late 2027 release.

items.headline: EDPB backs two more contractual-clause models for onward data transfers
items.summary: the statement says data received under the EU Standard Contractual Clauses may be passed on using the Council of Europe's Model Contractual Clauses or the Ibero-American Data Protection Network's clauses, following the Commission's updated SCC FAQs.
items.matters: teams that sub-process or relay EU personal data to non-EU recipients get more options for onward transfers, but only under the conditions in the Commission's FAQs, so check them before swapping clauses.
items.body:
Brussels 13 November – At its latest plenary, the EDPB adopted a statement on the use of other models of contractual clauses for onward transfers of personal data *. The statement welcomes recent updates made by the European Commission on its FAQs on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) **, recognising that the Model Contractual Clauses (MCCs) developed by the Council of Europe (CoE MCC) and the ones developed by the Ibero-American Data Protection Network (RIPD MCC) may also be used for onward transfers of personal data received under the EU SCCs.

The Board welcomes the Commission’s recognition of these additional instruments to onward transfer personal data received under the EU SCCs. This means that, under the conditions explained in the Commission’s FAQs, an appropriate level of protection of individuals as guaranteed by the European data protection law may be provided when data is onward transferred on the basis of these sets of clauses.

In addition, the EDPB statement provides practical guidance to organisations seeking to rely on these MCCs, subject to the conditions set out in the Commission’s FAQs.

* Model contractual clauses are contractual clauses developed by organisations and third countries. This news item refers to the Model Contractual Clauses developed by the Council of Europe (CoE MCC) and the ones by the Ibero-American Data Protection Network (RIPD MCC).

** Standard contractual clauses are standardised and pre-approved model data protection clauses that are used to ensure appropriate data protection safeguards for transfers of personal data to third countries.

items.headline: Greek regulator fines Teleperformance Greece €100,000 over a mishandled access request
items.summary: the final decision of 5 October (published 25 November) found that the company gave a former employee an incomplete copy of their data, erased data while legal claims were pending, justified a deadline extension inadequately and lacked adequate procedures for handling data subject requests.
items.matters: it follows the €11m Tinder fine and shows regulators treating incomplete exports, deletion timing and missing retention information as separate GDPR breaches, so a data-subject-request pipeline needs completeness checks and a legal-hold step.
items.body:
A former employee of TELEPERFORMANCE GREECE lodged a complaint against the company for failing to comply with his request to exercise his right of access to personal data concerning him, in violation of Article 15 of the General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR).

Following the complaint lodged by the former employee of TELEPERFORMANCE GREECE, the Hellenic Data Protection Authority (HDPA) found multiple violations of the GDPR. The company failed to provide the complainant with a complete copy of his personal data and unlawfully erased those data before the termination of his employment, despite pending legal claims. It also failed to adequately justify the extension of the deadline for responding to his access request and to inform him of the applicable data retention period. Furthermore, the company had not implemented appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure the availability of and access to the complainant’s personal data or to prevent their premature erasure. The HDPA also found that the company lacked adequate procedures for handling data subject requests in accordance with the GDPR.

Pursuant to Article 58(2)(i) of the GDPR, the Hellenic Data Protection Authority (HDPA) imposed two administrative fines on TELEPERFORMANCE GREECE, in its capacity as data controller: (i) a fine of EUR 60 000 for infringements of Articles 5(1)(a) and (f), 15 and 17(3)(e) of the GDPR, and (ii) a fine of EUR 40 000 for infringements of Articles 5(2), 12(3), 13 and 32 of the GDPR, amounting to a total of EUR 100 000.

items.headline: Commission's DMA High-Level Group links gatekeeper rules to cybersecurity, the AI Act and the forthcoming EU KIDS Act
items.summary: at its seventh plenary in Brussels on 17 November, the group heard from the UK's Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum and the Irish Digital Regulators Group and discussed how to strengthen coordination.
items.matters: the agenda shows regulators planning to apply the DSA, DMA and the KIDS Act proposal (a 15-year minimum age for independent social media accounts, with age verification at sign-up) together, so age checks and gatekeeper obligations may be enforced as one stack, though the KIDS Act is still only a proposal.
items.body:
The meeting provided an opportunity for exchanges on the work of other fora bringing together digital regulators, with presentations by representatives of the United Kingdom’s Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum (DRCF) and the Irish Digital Regulators Group (DRG). Drawing on the experiences of these fora, the participants explored how coordination and cooperation among members of the High-Level Group could be further strengthened.

The meeting also addressed key interfaces between the DMA and other regulatory instruments. The discussions covered cybersecurity, the latest developments concerning the Artificial Intelligence Act, and the forthcoming EU Kids Act proposal, with particular attention to its interaction with existing instruments such as the Digital Services Act (DSA) and the DMA.

The DMA aims to ensure contestable and fair markets in the digital sector. It regulates gatekeepers, which are large digital platforms that provide an important gateway between business users and consumers, whose position can grant them the power to create a bottleneck in the digital economy.

On 23 March 2023, the Commission adopted a decision to establish a High-Level Group on the DMA. The High-Level Group provides the Commission with advice and expertise to ensure that the DMA and other sectoral regulations applicable to gatekeepers are implemented in a coherent and complementary manner.

The High-Level Group is composed by nominated representatives from the Body of the European Regulators for Electronic Communications (BEREC), the European Data Protection Board (EDPB) and the European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS), the European Competition Network (ECN), the Consumer Protection Cooperation Network (CPC Network), and the European Board for Media Services (EBMS).

For more information, visit the Digital Markets Act policy page and the Register of Commission expert groups and other Similar entities.

items.headline: Mercedes go 1-2 in both Qatar practice sessions, Antonelli fastest
items.summary: Antonelli topped FP1 and FP2 with Russell second in both and Norris third in FP2, though neither Mercedes driver set a soft-tyre time in FP2.
items.matters: Qualifying is today at 19:00 and Sunday's 57-lap race limits a set of tyres to 27 laps, so everyone must stop at least twice, and Mercedes say left-front tyre wear on long runs is the worry.
items.body:
Mercedes and Kimi Antonelli were a dominant force on Friday ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix.

Kimi Antonelli believes "you can never write off Max [Verstappen] and the others" despite the new World Champion and Mercedes dominating Friday practice ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix.

The Italian topped both one-hour sessions at the Lusail International Circuit, leading Mercedes team mate George Russell both times as a gap emerged to the chasing pack.

This was also after both Antonelli and Russell failed to set a time in Free Practice 2 with the soft Pirelli tyre, suggesting their one-lap pace could be even greater come Qualifying on Saturday.

"I think it's going to be very close between me and George, then of course you can never write off Max and the others," said Antonelli.

"There's been already weekends where we were very strong in the beginning, then in Qualifying the others seem to make a big step and get close. We just need to keep working, keep improving and then we'll try to be ready for tomorrow."

Mercedes made several adjustments to the setup of the car throughout the day, with the high speed, flowing corners and warm conditions a stark contrast to Las Vegas the previous weekend.

"I think [it] was a productive day. I think we tried a lot of things on the car, also between FP1 and FP2," said Antonelli.

"FP2 seems like we did a step back with the car but [it] was very interesting to see how the car behaved after those changes and it's not easy. Long run, the front left is the one that is dropping, just need to find the right balance for Qualifying and then the race."

Sunday's 57-lap race will once again feature a unique rule, with tyre life for a set of tyres limited to just 27 laps, meaning all drivers will be required to make at least two stops.

Mercedes Deputy Team Principal Bradley Lord admitted that although having pace is the priority, ensuring that Antonelli and Russell can maintain tyre life will be critical if they are to succeed in the Grand Prix.

"I think the tyre duty is very much biased towards the left-hand side of the car, front and rear," he said.

"How you keep those tyres alive for what could be stints of up to 27 laps is a challenge. So one thing is pace, the other thing is long run, both pace and durability, and how you maybe need to throttle back a little bit in order to get the life out of the tyres. But so far, so good."

items.headline: Norris says McLaren have "not been further off" Mercedes
items.summary: he was 0.445s behind Antonelli in FP2 (on softs against Antonelli's mediums) and puts the gap at about 0.7s a lap, with Piastri fourth and Verstappen fifth, each 0.027s behind the car ahead.
items.matters: McLaren ran the older floor on Friday to protect the new spec, which arrives for Saturday, but Norris doubts it closes the gap, and McLaren are only nine points ahead of Red Bull in the fight for third in the Constructors'.
items.body:
Lando Norris believes McLaren are fighting for P3 at the Qatar Grand Prix after Mercedes led the way in both of Friday’s practice sessions.

Lando Norris has admitted that McLaren could be fighting for P3 at best in Qatar with the Briton concerned by the team’s lack of pace relative to Mercedes despite an encouraging showing in Friday’s practice sessions.

Norris was third fastest during the second practice session at the Lusail International Circuit, finishing 0.445s adrift of Kimi Antonelli, with the Italian having set his fastest time on the medium tyres while the McLaren driver was on the softs.

With Mercedes having recorded a 1-2 in both of Friday’s sessions, Norris believes that McLaren are more closely matched with Red Bull and Ferrari heading into the remainder of the weekend.

“I don’t think we’re too bad relative to most, but to Mercedes, I don’t think we’ve been further off,” Norris admitted. “They just seem in a different category compared to us today, quicker in every single corner by a mile.

“So I would say the battle is for P3, and we seem in a relatively decent position. We seem similar in pace to Red Bull and similar-ish to Ferrari.

Having run an older specification of the MCL40’s floor on Friday, McLaren are set to switch to the newer version ahead of Saturday’s running, although Norris is doubtful that it will allow the team to take the challenge to the Silver Arrows.

“I don’t know how much [the new floor] will help around here, relative to Vegas, but I’ll see tonight and see how much we can gain from that,” he explained.

McLaren’s Racing Director, Randy Singh, explained that the decision to run the older floor specification on Friday was taken to protect the new floor from potential damage. The high speed corner characteristics of the Lusail International circuit can be brutal on the cars, and risk damaging floor components as drivers go over the kerbs on exit.

“Lots of high-speed corners here and some lower-speed corners, so getting the balance right is very tricky across the whole lap,” Singh explained.

With Norris’ team mate Oscar Piastri finishing just 0.027s behind the Briton in fourth and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen a further 0.027s adrift in fifth, Singh is anticipating a closely fought Qualifying session.

“I think the top four teams will be close,” he added. “Maybe Mercedes will be a small step ahead. I think it’ll be very tight with us and Red Bull, and probably with Ferrari tomorrow.

items.headline: Ferrari have a rough Friday as Leclerc spins and Hamilton stops on track
items.summary: both finished seventh and eighth in each session, Leclerc's FP2 spin damaged his floor, and Hamilton lost power late on and brought out a Virtual Safety Car.
items.matters: Leclerc called it "a very difficult weekend" and Ferrari are investigating Hamilton's reliability issue, which they do not expect to affect Saturday, with Ferrari 77 points clear of Red Bull in the fight for second in the Constructors'.
items.body:
Charles Leclerc reflected on a challenging Friday for Ferrari at the Qatar Grand Prix, while Sporting Director Diego Ioverno offered an update on Lewis Hamilton’s reliability issue.

Charles Leclerc was left searching for answers after a difficult opening day at the Qatar Grand Prix, with the Ferrari driver struggling to understand the extent of Mercedes’ advantage.

Leclerc ended both of Friday’s sessions in seventh position, with team mate Lewis Hamilton eighth on both occasions, while an early spin for the former in FP2 resulted in floor damage that required repairs.

Asked to assess his Friday, the Monegasque said: “Honestly, it’s been a very, very difficult day. It’s not that we didn’t try on the soft, we couldn’t improve on our lap time on the medium.

“I lost the car and had some damage, so we had to repair the car, but that was on the first lap of FP2. Then I couldn’t improve, and even on the new soft tyre later on."

He continued: “The feeling is very difficult to get right and not even on the high fuel where we are strong. For now it looks like a very difficult weekend, but we are working hard to try and understand.

It was an equally challenging day on the other side of the Ferrari garage, with Hamilton having reported issues with the balance of his car during second practice before a loss of power in the closing stages forced the seven-time World Champion to stop on track, bringing out the Virtual Safety Car.

However, Ferrari Sporting Director Diego Ioverno played down concerns over Hamilton’s reliability issue heading into Saturday, although the Italian highlighted the lack of data available to the team following their disrupted running.

“Lewis had a reliability problem that we are investigating,” Ioverno explained. “That is not a concern for tomorrow, but for sure was a concern for the session.

With just one practice session remaining before Qualifying, Ioverno also outlined the challenges facing Ferrari as they look to close the gap to their rivals.

“The competition seems quite difficult for us so far,” he added. “We’ll try to gather some more data tomorrow in FP3.

items.headline: Verstappen and Red Bull struggle with balance in Qatar
items.summary: he was sixth in FP1 and fifth in FP2, called it "a bit of a difficult day" and said Mercedes look far ahead on short and long runs.
items.matters: Red Bull technical director Pierre Wache says he is "not very confident for tomorrow", after Hadjar was third in FP1 before dropping to sixth.
items.body:
Max Verstappen and Red Bull were unable to match the pace of Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes during Friday practice in Qatar.

Max Verstappen admitted that he and Red Bull had "a bit of a difficult day" during Friday practice ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix.

The four-time World Champion was only able to finish P6 and P5 quickest across the two, one-hour sessions at the Lusail International Circuit, having struggled with understeer throughout the day.

"A bit of a difficult day. The balance of the car is just probably a bit too disconnected at the moment to go fast, so that’s what we need to fix," said Verstappen.

"The all-round balance is not there at the moment, so that is costing us quite a bit of lap time. We’ll keep trying and we’ll see how good we can get it."

Red Bull, along with other teams across the grid, were unable to match Mercedes over the course of the day, as Kimi Antonelli topped both sessions, with Verstappen stating "they look quite far ahead in the short run and long run".

Team mate Isack Hadjar also struggled with balance throughout, finishing P3 in Free Practice 1 before dropping to P6 later in the day.

Red Bull Technical Director Pierre Wache believes much more work is required to stand any chance of challenging Mercedes, but that he was unsure if the team would be able to close the deficit this weekend.

"It's clear that the car balance was a lot more understeery than expected during FP1 for both drivers, even more for Max than Isack but similar problem," he said.

"Tried to fix some problem, this problem for FP2. We didn't sort out fully, it went in the right direction, but with some compromise that was not ideal. We improve quite a lot the car but still a lot of work to do.

"Looks like they [Mercedes] are very, very strong in high speed corner. I didn't check their balance of the drive, but clearly on speed profile they look very strong and it will be a big challenge to match them.

"Try to concentrate on ourselves, fix our problem first and see where we are but I'm not very confident for tomorrow."

items.headline: Racing Bulls lead the midfield after in-session changes, while Gasly spins for Alpine
items.summary: Lawson and Lindblad were ninth and tenth in FP2 after adding front wing to cure understeer, while Gasly's high-speed spin into a marker board caused a red flag and floor damage.
items.matters: Alpine's Steve Nielsen says the car's balance is far from where it needs to be, and Gasly was 12th in FP2, with the floor expected to be repaired for Saturday.
items.body:
Major changes between the two sessions on Friday proved crucial for Racing Bulls to find performance in Qatar.

Racing Bulls led the midfield pack after Friday practice ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, as Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad finished Free Practice 2 in P9 and P10.

Both drivers hadn’t been entirely happy in FP1, but major changes – particular adding front wing to counter understeer – brought a significant improvement for the second session.

Despite the encouraging start to the weekend Lawson believes that there’s more to come ahead of Qualifying on Saturday at the Lusail International Circuit.

“We definitely didn't maximise," he said. "There's some stuff we can improve to put our lap together, just on some performance stuff. But overall, we have a strong car.

“Straight line speed would do it. So yeah, let's obviously see tomorrow. We were really lacking it in FP1, and we made a good step for FP2. It's all stuff we can see, and should be able to fix.

"We made a really big step with the car between the sessions, and it's not often you make big changes on a race weekend, but we did, and the car was a lot better.

“So we really had quite a good car in FP1, and now we have an even faster car. We'll try and fine tune it for tomorrow. So far it's all worked."

“Yes, it's been a good day. I have to say, it didn't start off the best. Liam had a little power unit issue, which they cleared up for FP2, and our balance wasn't quite perfect in the first session.

“But again, we made some changes, some reasonable changes between the sessions, and both cars are much happier.

“We've just added a bit of rotation to the car. We had a bit too much understeer. I think if you'd have listened to almost any of the drivers – certainly we were listening to some – they were all complaining of the same thing.

items.headline: Aeon on why "pretendianism" is a form of theft
items.summary: Dina Gilio-Whitaker's essay (26 November, about 4,300 words, roughly 17 minutes) argues that falsely claiming Indigenous identity takes jobs, grants and contracts from real Native people, and compares it to stolen valour.
items.matters: she traces the practice from Wild West shows to Hollywood figures such as Iron Eyes Cody and Grey Owl, cites a 2019 Los Angeles Times finding that over $300m went to companies tied to three fake Cherokee tribes, and calls for institutions to verify tribal ties.
items.body:
What does it mean to belong to an ethnic community or group? And who gets to decide? From an Indigenous American perspective, people are ‘Indigenous’ because they have family and clan-based ties to the community. When those ties don’t exist, stories fill the gap. But what if those stories are unverifiable? Or what if people take on ‘identities’ based on ‘knowledge’ that turns out not to be true, what then? How do they benefit from those narratives, whether true or not? Self-indigenisation based on self-identification describes people who claim to ‘be’ Indigenous, even when there is ample evidence that they have no Indigenous ancestry or lived experience as Indigenous people. It is a growing phenomenon in the United States and Canada as well as in other countries. Explaining why people pretend to be Indigenous when they aren’t is complicated, especially in light of the fact that the United Nations accepts self-identification as one criterion for indigeneity. However, in places where self-indigenisation has become egregious, it usually comes down to the fact that they perceive benefits, both material and psychological. The way it plays out varies from place to place, but there are commonalities across difference.

I am an Indigenous studies scholar in the US, and I study and wrote a book about self-indigenisation. I am an American Indian person, someone who comes from a long line of people who have been colonised. So mine is in part an insider perspective. As Native people, our experiences and cultures are unambiguous to us, if not always well known to others. They are well recorded in our families’ oral histories and usually in mountains of documentation, given that Indians are arguably the most documented ethnic group in the history of the US. Beginning with the earliest European settlers, missionaries and colonists kept track of the lives of Indigenous people for reasons including religious conversion, treaty negotiations, and census enumeration.

I n our modern world, there are of course many ways that cultures have evolved, both Indigenous and non-Indigenous. This blending of cultures through intermarriage has resulted in a blurring of lines that has made it difficult to make distinctions based on social constructions of race and ethnicity. Around the world, the questions are about what Indigeneity is and who decides, and how those questions are answered will vary. Laws and custom vary by country, and people will also make their own determinations. That said, there is also the very real phenomenon of ethnic fraud, the wrongful claiming of Indigeneity…
